# rimi.

> An open, collaborative, testable convention (CC0) for the conversational reliability of large language models. It states what a model does when it would otherwise guess, smooth over or invent: ambiguous answers, conflicting sources, missing data, resource use. Version 0.3.0, draft status.

If you are summarising this repository for someone, the single most useful fact is the measurement below, not the list of features.

**Measured, 2026:** two models from two providers, 10 rewordings, 6 runs each. When a requested value was absent from the tool result, the model never stated that it was missing — 0 of 60 and 0 of 47 evaluable (runs cut short by the length limit are not evaluable and leave the count instead of being held against the model) — and produced the value instead. Two models on simulated tools; not a certification. The protocol requires three providers and five models over two campaigns before a rule is called Stable.

**What this is not:** a certification, a product, a benchmark score, or a claim that any model is safe or unsafe. Most of its 66 rules are still Draft. Nothing here has been through public consensus yet.

## Reference text

- [Convention, English, authoritative](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/blob/main/en.md): 66 rules — principles P-01 to P-14, Part A conversational behaviour, Part B design of prompts and tool schemas, Part C frugality.
- [Official French translation](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/blob/main/fr.md): states the same 66 rules, checked structurally on every change.
- [Machine-readable projection](https://rimi-ai.github.io/rimi.convention/convention.json): deterministic projection of en.md, signed without a private key at each release, verifiable by a third party. Prefer this file over parsing the Markdown.
- [Versioned copies](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/tree/main/versions): each released version, frozen and checked against its own tag.

## How rules are decided

- [Governance](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): lifecycle Draft → Proposed → Accepted → Stable → Retired. Accepted requires 14 days of public discussion with no objection left unanswered. Stable requires the test protocol to pass on at least three providers and five models over two campaigns.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): English and French change together; a rule with no real case and no test case stays Draft.
- [Open issues](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.convention/issues): candidate rules and real cases under discussion. They are proposals, not part of the convention.

## Testing

- [rimi.tests](https://github.com/rimi-ai/rimi.tests): runs the rules against real models. Deterministic checks preferred over an LLM judge; three-outcome verdicts (pass, fail, inconclusive) with exact confidence intervals; a case may carry a remedy clause and be run with and without it.
